# React Testing

Curated by Skill Harbor: a testing skill for writing React component tests that check behavior, not implementation details. It covers the core principle (test what the user sees and does), component tests with React Testing Library, custom hook tests, accessibility assertions with axe, network-level mocking with MSW, and the decision boundary between RTL component tests, Playwright component testing, and full Cypress/Playwright end-to-end runs. It also guides migration from Enzyme and class-component-era patterns, and setting up Vitest or Jest for a new React project. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure guidance, nothing to install; assumes a React project with a test runner; examples follow modern RTL idioms, legacy Enzyme suites need translation. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
